name: Obayashi fireproof coating spray robot (2nd generation)
summary: Self-moving robot with a six-axis arm on a lifting and sideways carriage that sprays semi-dry rockwool fireproof coating onto steel beams on building sites. Developed by the Japanese contractor Obayashi for its own projects; the second generation went into use in Tokyo in November 2023.

germany.statusNote: Not sold: Obayashi developed the robot for its own construction sites in Japan. It says it hopes other companies will use such spray robots in future, but no sale, rental or licence offer was found, in Germany or elsewhere.

specs.label: Coating thickness
specs.quote: The robot can spray fireproof coatings for one-hour protection (25 mm thick), two-hour protection (45 mm thick), and three-hour protection (60 mm thick)

specs.label: Spraying method
specs.value: semi-dry rockwool (rockwool and cement slurry mixed at the nozzle)
specs.quote: Semi-dry rockwool spraying methodA method for applying fireproof coating in which rockwool and cement slurry are mixed together at the tip of a spray nozzle and sprayed onto a steel surface.

specs.label: Components
specs.value: travel device, lifting device, transverse device, six-axis industrial robot arm
specs.quote: Travel device, lifting device, transverse deviceSix-axis industrial robot arm

specs.label: Output
specs.value: about the same area per day as a skilled sprayer
specs.conditions: maker statement for the robot family
specs.quote: The fireproof coating spray robots can spray roughly the same area per day as a skilled sprayer

notes: Moves autonomously along pre-registered task data to each spraying position and starts spraying; the second generation fixes its position with the resection method used in surveying.
From April 2024 a measuring function senses the steel beams and corrects the relative error between robot and beam before spraying (maker plan).
500 mm narrower and 500 kg lighter than the 2019 first generation, so it fits temporary site lifts more easily.
Travel device named by the maker; wheels assumed, not stated.

evidence.task: Sprays rockwool fireproof coating onto the steel beams of office buildings; expected to coat over 9,000 m² by the end of FY2023
evidence.note: First-generation robots (2019) were already in use on several medium- to high-rise office projects.

sources.title: Obayashi Develops a New Fireproof Coating Spray Robot for Wider Use on Construction Sites (29 January 2024)

openQuestions: Has Obayashi offered the robot to other contractors, as it says it hopes to? No offer or price found.
Spraying rate per hour and crew size are not stated, only 'roughly the same area per day as a skilled sprayer'.
No use-case id fits fireproof coating of steel beams; evidence has no taskIds.
